 COMMON JUDGMENT
These petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V Act seeking compensation for the injuries caused in a road traffic accident.
Both petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment.

2. The case of the petitioner is that on 06-02-2021 at about 11.00 p.m., when the petitioners were proceeding in Baleno car to Goa trip and left Hosakote and and the said car was driven by its driver Vikas Via Bengaluru, Tumkur, Sira, Hiriyur NH 04 towards Goa, Hosuru village, Metikurke,
Hiriyur, at about 4.30 a.m. drove the car in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the said car and dashed against on going lorry in front of the said car and due to the said impact sustained severe injuries and took treatment at Government hospital, Sanjay Gandhi institute of Trauma and orthopaedics, Bengaluru as inpatient and discharged with an advice to take complete bed rest and followup treatment.

sentences.text: The petitioners spent money for their treatment.
The petitioner (in MVC No.2696/21) was working in a private firm and earning Rs.30,000/-p.m.

The petitioner (in MVC No.2695/21) was working in a private firm and earning Rs.25,000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries, petitioners in both case are unable to do their normal work and lost the income.
Hence prays to award the compensation of Rs.15 lakhs each in both cases from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Tribunal and filed their respective written statement.
4. Respondent No.1 filed objections which is common in both cases, has contended that, petition is manifestly vexatious and merits less in the sense it does not disclose a clear rights to sue.

The RC owner of the cab bearing No.KA- 03-AC-9809 and it is insured with the 2nd respondent and same was valid from 10-5-2020 to 9-5-2021 and the same is in force as on the accident and driver of the said vehicle is having valid DL to drive the same as such, if any compensation amount award by this court, that is payable by the insurer o the vehicle only i.e., the 2 nd respondent only.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant without any basis.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
The 2nd respondent filed written statement wherein contended that owner and insurer of the third party unknown lorry not been made as parties to the proceedings.
The driver of the insured vehicle was not having valid and effective DL to drive the same.
The 1 st respondent has allowed a person who was not having valid DL to drive the same as on the date of alleged accident.
There was no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle in issue as he was proceeding with due care and cautious by following the traffic rules and regulations.

There is a violation of Section 134(c)

No.KA-03-AG- 9809 on the same day as per Ex-P2.

Thereafter jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex-P1,
thereafter after conducting the thorough and detailed investigation has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle Baleno car for the offence punishable u/s 279, 337, 338, 304A of IPC by holding that on 7-2-2021 at about 2.30 a.m. near gate of Hosur village in the NH 4 from Deekshith M vs Orix Auto Infrastructure on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163033721/

13. Further on perusal of the Ex-P4 spot mahazar, the spot of accident was the NH 4 Tar road near Hosur gate from Hiriyur towards Chitradurga and width of the road was 36 feet running from south to north, straight road.
Further on perusal of Ex-P5 it clearly shows that accident has been taken place on the extreme left side of the road.
The very manner of the accident clearly establishes that the accident has been taken place due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Baleno car.
Even respondent has not examined either driver of the car or driver of the lorry to prove their contention.
Hence the respondent failed to prove their contention that accident has been take place due to sole rash driving of the driver of the unknown lorry.
Moreover no evidence and materials were placed on record by the respondent to prove that the charge sheet filed by the police is collusive and defective.

14. Further though respondent No.2 counsel contended that the driver of the insured vehicle and the petitioners were under the influence of the alcohol at the time of the accident and thereby violated the conditions of the policy, but no evidence and materials were placed on record by the respondent to prove that either of the petitioners or the driver of the insured vehicle were under the influence of alcohol.
Further jurisdictional police after thorough investigation has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle only for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 and 304A of IPC.
No where investigation officer during his investigation found any evidence with regard to the fact that driver of the offending vehicle Baleno car was under the influence of the alcohol.

Even the medical reports, wound certificate Ex-P7 of the Dikshith and discharge summary of the DiksithEx-P8 and 9 and OPD Ex-P10, 11 and 12 of the Dikshth does not reveals about any consumption of alcohol by the petitioner.

The second respondent has not produced any medical reports of the driver of the offending vehicle to establish that at the time of the accident, driver of the offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol.

In the absence of any evidence and materials on record this court cannot believe the contention of the resplendent No.2.
15.
Further Ex-P15 wound certificate of the Dileep and Ex-P16 discharge summary of the Dileep there is no mention about the consumption of alcohol by the said Dileep.
Even the respondent No.2 has not produced any document to show that the driver of the insured vehicle Vikas was under the influence of the alcohol at the time of the accident.
Hence respondent No.2 failed to prove that respondent No.1 has violated the policy conditions by allowing the persons to drive the vehicle under the influence of the alcohol.

sentences.text: "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
17. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 and 2 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
18. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 and 2 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

19. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

30. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., (1) Cut Lacerated Wound over left upper eyelid region (2) Diffuse oedema over left eye and (3) Multiple facial bone.

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card, it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner as 09.04.1997 and the accident took place on 06.02.2021.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 24 years.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to the accident he was doing work in a private firm viz. Mitra Online Company and earning Rs.30,000/-p.m. and lost the earnings.

Though the petitioner Deekshith M., contended that he was working in Private firm Mitra Online Company an drawing salary of Rs.30,000/- and also getting overtime allowances, but he has not examined any HR of the said company or any of the officer of the said company to prove the same.

But, the petitioner has produced Bank statement as per Ex.P14.
As per Ex.P14, the petitioner was working in Aspino HR Services and was drawing salary of Rs.21,866/- in the month of February 2021.
Even the petitioner has produced his ID Card, as per which, the petitioner was working in Aspino HR Services limited from 22.09.2020.

Hence, Ex.P14 cannot be relied on.
